title: At a loose end
titleZh: 现代社会是如何让英国年轻人对职场毫无准备的？
summary:
至少从解散修道院运动、英国政府首次直接承担当时被称为“救济”的事务时起，福利政策的核心便一直存在某种难以调和的矛盾：对个人提供的外部支持越多，人们就越容易对这种支持形成依赖。

来源：The Critic；作者：Henry Hill；原文发布时间：2026-04-27 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Since at least the dissolution of the monasteries, when the English state first assumed direct responsibility for what was then called “alms”, there has been an irreconcilable tension at the heart of welfare policy: that the more external support you provide people, the more dependent on such support they tend to become.
paragraphs.contentZh: 至少从解散修道院运动、英国政府首次直接承担当时被称为“救济”的事务时起，福利政策的核心便一直存在某种难以调和的矛盾：对个人提供的外部支持越多，人们就越容易对这种支持形成依赖。

paragraphs.contentEn: That the Starmer Government is no closer to finding a sustainable equilibrium on this point is made clear by the latest intervention from Alan Milburn, the former New Labour minister now heading up the latest enquiry into youth unemployment and inactivity. Per the Financial Times, he is determined to draw attention to the role of parents; according to the research he’s drawing on, children more likely to become “NEETS” (Not in Education, Employment, or Training) can be identified at age five.
paragraphs.contentZh: 从前新工党大臣艾伦·米尔本的最新表态来看，很明显，斯塔默政府在这一问题上仍未找到可持续的平衡点，米尔本目前正牵头一项针对青年失业与待业状况的最新调研。据《金融时报》报道，他正试图将讨论焦点转向父母的作用；其所援引的研究显示，那些更有可能在日后成为“NEETs”（即不处在教育、就业或培训中的人）的儿童，早在五岁时就能够被识别出来。

paragraphs.contentEn: It all sounds very sensible. But it is difficult to reconcile a stern and unflinching view of inadequate parenting with some of the Government’s other policies. We are talking, after all, about a ministry which has made schools responsible for brushing children’s teeth. As so often, one can see the logic behind the proposals: if children aren’t brushing their teeth at home, it is better for their health to do it at school than not at all. The move is also — depressingly but not unsurprisingly — popular with parents. But it invites the question of at what point “support for families” crosses the line into simply replacing their proper functions.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这些说法听起来都颇为合理。但问题在于，政府一方面对家庭教育缺位持严厉且毫不妥协的立场，另一方面却推行着与之并不一致的政策，两者之间难以协调。毕竟，我们面对的，是一个甚至要求学校负责给孩子刷牙的政府部门。和以往一样，这类提议背后的逻辑并不难理解：既然孩子在家里不刷牙，那么出于健康考虑，让学校来做总好过完全不做。而且令人有些无奈却并不意外的是，这一举措在家长中颇受欢迎。而这自然引出了另一个问题：所谓“对家庭的支持”，是从哪一刻起已经越过了界限，变成了对家庭应有功能的直接替代？

paragraphs.contentEn: Any fearless look at the question of youth inactivity would need also at least to consider all the ways in which modern society contrives to make young adults un-ready for work. There is nothing natural or inevitable about it, after all. Historically, people stepped into adult life in their mid-teens, and by their late teens were usually either in employment or, in the case of many women, assuming adult responsibilities in the home (and in a pre-modern home that was definitely work). Indeed, the entire concept of a “teenager” only really came about in the 1960s.
paragraphs.contentZh: 如果想要毫不回避地审视青年待业问题，就至少需要考量现代社会如何以各种方式在无形中导致年轻人无法为职场做好准备。毕竟，这种状态既非自然形成，也并非无可避免。从历史上看，人们通常在十五六岁便开始步入成人生活；到十七八岁，要么已经进入职场，要么——就许多女性而言——已经在家庭中承担起成年人的责任（在前现代社会的家庭语境中，这无疑也是实实在在的劳动）。事实上，“青少年”这一概念本身，也只是到20世纪60年代才真正出现。

paragraphs.contentEn: Yet today, many young people don’t even face any general expectation that they should enter the world of work until at least their early twenties. For many of those that pursue further or higher education, what might once have been a simple transition from a five-day school week to a five-day work week is broken up by several years in which they have very little structure at all. This suits some people very well, but there is little acknowledgement in education policy discussions about those whom it might not.
paragraphs.contentZh: 然而在当下，许多年轻人甚至在二十岁出头之前，都不再面临必须进入职场的普遍期待。对不少选择继续深造或接受高等教育的青年而言，以往从每周五天的学校生活到五天工作制的简单过渡，如今却被一段持续数年、期间几乎全无框架和约束的漫长岁月所切断。这样的安排对一部分人来说确实行之有效，但在围绕教育政策的讨论中，却鲜有人提及那些因此而无所适从的群体。

paragraphs.contentEn: As for those who don’t pursue tertiary education, many have been kept in school longer than is sensible. Having been set at 15 in 1947, the school leaving age was raised to 16 in 1972, and then 18 (including college) under the last Conservative government. This not only traps some people (particularly some boys) in an academic environment to which they are ill-suited, but seems very likely to have a psychological effect. When I was in Sixth Form, we were all cognisant that we had crossed some sort of threshold into adulthood — reinforced by the school extending us special privileges, such as leaving the campus — and were there as volunteers. That is not true today (and my old school no longer lets sixth formers leave the site).
paragraphs.contentZh: 至于那些没有选择接受高等教育的年轻人，许多人留在学校的时间也被延长到了未必合理的程度。英国的法定离校年龄在1947年定为15岁，1972年提高到16岁，而在上一届保守党政府时期，这一门槛（包括继续教育）又被进一步提高到18岁。这一变化不仅使一部分年轻人（尤其是一些男生）长期停留在并不适合他们的学术环境中，还很可能带来一定的心理影响。在我读第六年级（相当于高中最后两年）时，大家都清楚意识到自己已经迈入某种意义上的成年阶段——学校也通过给予一些特殊权限（例如允许离校）来强化这种感受——那时我们继续留在学校，更多是出于自愿选择。但如今情况已不再如此（就连我的母校现在也不再允许第六年级学生离校）。

paragraphs.contentEn: Is the Government likely to do anything about this? Unlikely. Imagine you headed a progressive government which had just made youth unemployment worse by hiking the minimum wage and bringing in onerous new workplace rights. Would you rather a) admit your mistake, and at the same time that endlessly raising the minimum wage has downsides, or b) justify more spending in order to “invest” in even more education and training for young people?
paragraphs.contentZh: 政府会在这个问题上采取行动吗？恐怕不太可能。试想一下，如果你执掌的是一个进步派政府，并且刚刚因为上调最低工资、推行繁苛的劳动权益新规，反而导致青年失业问题进一步恶化，你会怎么做？是a）承认政策失误，同时也承认不断提高最低工资并非没有代价；还是b）找理由增加更多开支，以“投资”为名为年轻人提供更多的教育和培训？

paragraphs.contentEn: It’s obviously going to be “b”, especially when state policy has for decades (even under the Tories) been built around doing just that. Consider again that acronym, “NEET”; by giving education and training equal billing with employment, it means that from an official perspective, shunting a young person onto a course (even one of dubious quality and significant expense) is equivalent to finding them work. But don’t worry, nobody can say the Prime Minister isn’t alive to the challenges facing young people. Banning chicken nuggets from the cafeteria ought to do the trick. Right?
paragraphs.contentZh: 答案显然会是“b”，尤其是在过去几十年里（即便是在保守党执政时期），国家政策本就一直围绕着这个逻辑来构建。再看“NEET”这个缩略词；它将教育、培训与就业并列，本身就意味着在官方语境中，把一个年轻人随意塞进某个课程（即便课程质量存疑、成本不低），在某种程度上就等同于为其解决了就业问题。当然，也不能说首相没有关注年轻人面临的难题。把食堂里的炸鸡块下架，问题大概就解决了吧？对吗？
